overview.body:
**Tōnatiuh** ​(*tonatiuh*) — ‌Sun, ‌Heat, Fifth ​Age · ​He ​who goes ​forth ​shining; the ‌Nahuatl ​sun god ​— belongs ‌to ​the Nahuatl ‌tradition, ​where it ‌is ​catalogued under ​the domain ​"Sun, ​Heat, Fifth ​Age". ‌The name ​means ‌"He who ​goes ‌forth shining; ​the Nahuatl ‌sun ​god"[^1].

**Tōnatiuh** ‌belongs ​to the ​Nahuatl ‌tradition, where ‌it is ‌associated ​with sun, ​heat, ‌fifth age.[^2]

​PuniCodex ​restores the ‌name as ​**Tōnatiuh** ​and serves ‌its ​temple at ‌[tonatiuh.com](https://punicodex.com/tonatiuh/). ​The restoration ​preserves at ​least ​one distinctive ‌feature ‌— a ​diacritic ‌or a ​distinctive letter ​— ‌that the ‌ASCII ‌form loses, ‌and ​exactly one ‌historically valid ​Unicode ​restoration exists, ​which ‌places the ​name ​in Tier ​1. ‌The plain ​ASCII form ​*tonatiuh* ​survives as ‌a ​modern convenience ‌imposed ​by the ‌early domain-name ​system; ‌the restoration, ‌not ​the fallback, ​is ​the form ​the project ‌defends ‌as philologically ​complete[^2].

the-name.body:
The name ​is attested ‌in the ‌colonial alphabetic ​corpus and ​in logographic writing ​in the ​codices; the ​restoration uses ‌the normalized ​scholarly orthography. Etymologically ​the name ‌means "He ​who goes ‌forth shining; ​the Nahuatl sun ‌god"[^1].

Classical ​Nahuatl Tōnatiuh, ​the sun; ​the fifth ​sun of the ​Aztec cosmos, ‌born from ​the sacrifice ‌of Nanahuatzin.

The ​ASCII form ‌*tonatiuh* survives ​only because ‌the early ​domain-name system could ‌not carry ​diacritics; it ​is a ‌technological compromise, ‌not an ancient ‌spelling. The ​Unicode restoration ​**Tōnatiuh** recovers ‌the vowel ​length of the ​original directly ‌in the ​address bar. ​The restoration ‌preserves at least ​one distinctive ‌feature — ​a diacritic ​or a ​distinctive letter — ​that the ‌ASCII form ‌loses, and ​exactly one ‌historically valid Unicode ​restoration exists, ​which places ‌the name ‌in Tier ‌1.

The letter-by-letter ‌transformation runs:

​- **t** ‌→ **T** ​— Same, ​capitalized
- **o** ​→ **ō** ‌— Macron: ​long vowel
​- **n** → ​**n** — ‌Same
- ​**a** → ​**a** — ​Same
- **t** ‌→ **t** ​— Same
‌- **i** ​→ **i** ‌— Same
- ​**u** → ‌**u** — ‌Same
- ​**h** → ​**h** — Same

​The canonical ​temple for ‌this name ‌is served ​at **tonatiuh.com**[^2].

pronunciation.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation ‌of ​the ​name is ​**/tonatiuh/** ​— ​Nahuatl ‌Reconstruction.[^1]

​Phoneme ​by ‌phoneme:

​- ‌**T** ​— Initial ‌character ​of ​the ​restored ​form ​Tōnatiuh.
‌- ​**ōnatiuh** ‌— Remainder ​of ‌the ​name, ‌preserving ​the ‌distinctive ​marks ​of ‌the ‌Nahuatl tradition.

‌For ​the ​modern ‌speaker, ​the ​closest ‌approximation ​is: ​'TONATIUH' ‌— pronounce ​the ‌restored ​form ​with ​attention ​to ‌the ‌preserved ​diacritics ‌and length.

​Kindred ​and ‌historical ‌forms ‌of ‌the ​name:

‌- ​**Nahuatl** ​— Tōnatiuh, ​the ‌restored ​Unicode ​form ​of ‌the ​name

​Tōnatiuh ​is Tier ‌1 ​because ‌the ​Nahuatl ‌form ​preserves ‌distinctive ‌features ​that ​ASCII loses: ​stress, ​length, ‌or ‌special ​characters.

mythology.body:
The ​stories of ‌**Tōnatiuh** circulate ‌within ​the Nahuatl ​corpus, where ​the ​figure embodies ​sun, heat, ‌fifth ​age.[^1]

### ​Primary Attestation ‌(Sources)

​Tōnatiuh is ‌attested in ​the ‌canonical Nahuatl ​sources as ​a ​figure associated ​with sun, ​heat, ‌fifth age.[^1]

​### ‌Name and ​Meaning (Etymology)

‌The ​name means ‌"He who ​goes ‌forth shining; ​the Nahuatl ​sun ‌god" and ‌reflects the ‌figure's ​role in ​the tradition. ‌**Tōnatiuh** ​is the ​Nahuatl sun ‌god, ​depicted as ​a warrior ‌ascending ​from the ‌east. The ​Aztecs ​believed that ​the present ​sun, ‌the Fifth ‌Sun, was ​born ‌when the ​gods sacrificed ​themselves ‌at Teotihuacan; ‌Tōnatiuh now ‌demands ‌blood sacrifice ​to continue ‌his ​daily journey.[^1] ​His face ​is ‌shown in ​the ​center of ​the Aztec ‌calendar ​stone. Tonatiuh's ​aged face ​and ‌tongue of ​obsidian knife ‌imagery ​stress that ‌the sun ​is ‌a warrior ‌who must ​be ​nourished by ​human hearts ​to ‌defeat the ‌forces of ​darkness.[^1]
